components.css: .ds-route { list-style: none; margin: 0; padding: 24px; width: 320px; background: var(--bg, #17110d); color: var(--text-2, #e4d8c9); } .ds-route li { position: relative; } .ds-route li:not(:last-child)::before { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 5px; top: 31px; height: 100%; width: 1px; background: rgba(243, 236, 226, 0.18); } .ds-route li:first-child::after { content: ''; position: absolute; left: 5px; top: 31px; height: 100%; width: 1px; background: var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.11 65)); } .ds-route a { position: relative; display: grid; grid-template-columns: 28px minmax(0, 1fr); grid-template-areas: 'n name' 'n meta'; column-gap: 14px; row-gap: 2px; padding: 14px 0 14px 26px; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(243, 236, 226, 0.1); color: inherit; text-decoration: none; } .ds-route li:last-child a { border-bottom: 0; } .ds-route a::before { content: ''; position: absolute; z-index: 1; left: 0; top: 26px; width: 11px; height: 11px; border-radius: 50%; box-sizing: border-box; border: 1.5px solid var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.11 65)); background: var(--bg, #17110d); transition: background 0.3s, transform 0.3s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); } .ds-route a.passed::before, .ds-route a[aria-current]::before { background: var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.11 65)); } .ds-route a[aria-current]::before { transform: scale(1.35); } .ds-route-n { grid-area: n; padding-top: 7px; font: 400 18px 'Instrument Serif', serif; color: var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.11 65)); } .ds-route b { grid-area: name; font: 400 30px/1.1 'Instrument Serif', serif; letter-spacing: -0.01em; transition: color 0.2s; } .ds-route small { grid-area: meta; font: 400 13px 'Hanken Grotesk', system-ui, sans-serif; color: var(--subtle, #a89a8a); } .ds-route a[aria-current] b { color: var(--text, #f3ece2); } .ds-route a:hover b { color: var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.11 65)); } .ds-route a:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, oklch(0.8 0.11 65)); outline-offset: 3px; }

narrative.overview:
A dimly lit table at the end of the evening: espresso ground, cream type, and one warm caramel light that falls only on the words worth leaning toward. The site reads like a printed food-and-travel supplement more than a creator link page. Large Instrument Serif headlines carry the voice, Hanken Grotesk carries the facts, and the caramel lives almost entirely in italics, ordinals and the one action the page wants.

Density is relaxed and editorial: wide section breathing room, hairline dividers instead of boxes, and the proof (9:16 video cards, view counts, partner brands) given the most surface. Depth comes from photographs, never from containers. The world is chic and restrained; ornaments are typographic (a thin caramel rule, a middot, a serif numeral), never decorative symbols.
keyCharacteristics: Espresso dark ground with one inverted cream band (portfolio) and one full-caramel band (contact).
Instrument Serif at weight 400 for every headline, title and number; italic phrases in caramel.
Pill-shaped actions; softly rounded 9:16 media; flat text surfaces divided by 1px hairlines.
Soft, dark, diffuse shadows only under photographs, the lightbox and floating actions.
The route: a vertical hairline with caramel stop dots that light as the reader passes them.

rules.name: The Caramel Speaks Once Rule
rules.body: On dark grounds caramel is reserved for italic emphasis, ordinals and route marks, data leads, and the primary action. Body copy, borders and surfaces never take it, except the contact band, where it becomes the ground.

rules.name: The Three Grounds Rule
rules.body: Espresso is the default, cream is the inverted proof band, caramel is the closing ask. Each ground swaps its accent: caramel on espresso, burnt caramel on cream, espresso on caramel (italics inherit). The focus ring follows the same swap (`--focus` set to espresso on cream and caramel).

rules.name: The Serif Counts Rule
rules.body: Every figure the brand should remember (followers, views, percentages, ordinals) is set in Instrument Serif at weight 400, with tabular numerals where numbers stack. The sans never sets a hero number.

rules.name: The Weightless Serif Rule
rules.body: Instrument Serif is only ever weight 400. Emphasis comes from italic and caramel, not bold.

rules.name: The Photographs Float Rule
rules.body: Only imagery and floating actions cast shadows. A block of text that needs separation gets a hairline or a band, never a drop shadow, and never a hard offset shadow.

dos: **Do** close serif headlines with an italic phrase in caramel (burnt caramel on cream, inherited espresso on caramel).
**Do** set every remembered number in Instrument Serif 400 and every label in Hanken Grotesk.
**Do** separate sections and rows with the 1px hairline or a tonal band before reaching for a container.
**Do** keep every action a pill with a 44px minimum target and the caramel-or-cream fill logic above.
**Do** present proof as 9:16 media cards with brand badge and views, in 14px-gap auto-fill grids.
**Do** honour reduced motion: marquee, fills, route transitions, card fades and the dock all stop.
donts: **Don't** use decorative symbols or kitsch ornaments (such as ✦) as separators; use the thin caramel rule, a middot or a slash.
**Don't** bold Instrument Serif or set it in any weight other than 400.
**Don't** put caramel on body copy, borders or surfaces on the espresso ground.
**Don't** cast shadows from text blocks, and never use a hard offset shadow.

**Don't** add uppercase tracked kickers above headlines on new surfaces; the niche pages ship without them and the uppercase label stays attached to items (card captions, lightbox category, brand tags).
**Don't** tilt route rows, grids or text; rotation belongs to the hero photo collage only.
